answer: Hypothesis: The domain is **Social** (the Social discipline, i.e., social psychology). Data evidence: at the study level (one row per original/replication pair; 74 Social studies), original studies used student subjects in 83.8% of cases (62/74) and replications in 81.1% (60/74) — the closest match to the reported 82.4%/80.9% (Euclidean distance 1.9 vs 48.0 for Cognitive and 509.9 for Economics). Social is the only domain in which BOTH original and replication primarily (majority, >50%, and modal category) use student subjects: Cognitive's original share is only 75.5% (row-level 71.4%) and Economics is far higher (94.4%/100.0%). The conclusion is robust to every tested scheme (row-level 927 rows: Social 82.0/78.4; drop==False subsets: 99.3/80.2 row-level, 93.8/85.9 study-level; missing-value denominator variants: 84.9/82.2) — Social wins under all of them.

payload.hypothesis: The domain in which both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects is the Social discipline (social psychology). Among the 74 Social-discipline studies, original studies used student subjects in 83.8% (62/74) and replications in 81.1% (60/74) — the closest match to the cited 82.4%/80.9% — and Social is the only domain where both original and replication are majority-student under every tested analysis scheme (Cognitive: 75.5%/81.6% study-level; Economics: 94.4%/100.0%).
payload.workflow: Loaded meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927 rows, 57 cols, 141 unique O/R-pair ids). Verified key fields: discipline (Social 668/Cognitive 241/Economics 18), subjects.o (students 737/anyone 143/community 46/1 NaN), subjects.r (students 744/online 148/community 25/anyone 9/1 NaN); no case/whitespace variants, no full-row or (id,lab_id) duplicates; single missing-subjects row rpp.154 (drop=True). Built the main study-level frame (one row per id: aggregated=True pooled rows for ml1/ml3, single rows for rpp/ee) and computed per-discipline shares of 'students' for subjects.o and subjects.r, with missing counted in the denominator. Ran sensitivity analyses: missing excluded from denominator, row-level (927 lab/single rows), and drop==False subsets, and selected the domain minimizing distance to (82.4, 80.9). The second dataset (replication_success) was inspected and found unnecessary (no subjects/discipline columns). Executed script: analysis.py.
